script: That classic head-down, side-eye, ears-back look your dog gives you when something's chewed up on the floor? Science says it's probably not guilt at all. Dogs are incredible at reading human body language, and that face is actually a learned reaction to your reaction, they've figured out that acting submissive the moment you use a certain tone makes the tension go away faster. It's less I feel bad and more I know you're upset and this usually works. Researchers have even shown dogs make that exact same face when they're accused of something they didn't even do, purely based on the owner's tone of voice, nothing else. So that guilty look isn't confession, it's just a really smart social strategy. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
